Midtjylland (Central Denmark Region) is one of the five administrative regions of [[danmark|Danmark]]. Within the context of the Danish healthcare system, it is a key geographical and administrative unit monitored by the Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) under the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme. The database tracks clinical quality indicators for acute, high-risk abdominal surgical patients, evaluating performance at the national, regional, and individual hospital levels. Midtjylland encompasses several major healthcare providers, including [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]], [[hospitalsenhed-midt|Hospitalsenhed Midt]], [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]], [[regionshospitalet-horsens|Regionshospitalet Horsens]], and [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] [^src4].

In terms of clinical performance, Midtjylland's results are closely tracked across multiple indicators. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which measures antibiotic treatment within three hours, the region achieved a compliance rate of 39.8% (95% CI: 35.9–43.6) during the period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, marking the second-highest regional result among the available data [^src1]. In the subsequent reporting period from September 1, 2023, to August 31, 2024, the region's compliance for Indikator 1 improved to 44.6% (95% CI: 40.8–48.4) [^src6]. 

The region's performance is also evaluated on more specialized and supplementary metrics. For [[indikator-5x|Indikator 5x]], which tracks the speed of surgical intervention for life-threatening conditions such as perforation, ischemia, or bleeding, 66 out of 243 patients in Midtjylland were operated on within six hours, yielding a compliance rate of 27.2% (95% CI: 21.7–33.2) [^src2]. Furthermore, when examining 30-day mortality following acute surgery among patients with mild to moderate comorbidity ([[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]]), Midtjylland recorded a mortality rate of 10.7% (24 out of 225 patients; 95% CI: 7.0–15.5) [^src4]. The region also reported a 13.9% compliance rate for early nutritional assessment (Indicator 8) during the 2022–2023 period [^src3].

When comparing patient demographics and baseline health statuses across the five Danish regions—[[hovedstaden|Hovedstaden]], Midtjylland, [[nordjylland|Nordjylland]], [[sjaelland|Sjælland]], and [[syddanmark|Syddanmark]]—analyses of the [[asa-score|ASA]] score and patient [[alder]] revealed no significant regional differences, indicating a relatively uniform distribution of patient risk profiles and demographics across the country [^src5].
